citation: Zabalo, Jacobo. "Notes on Boredom and Metaphysics, Sociologically Framed." Ars Brevis 25 (2019): 307-324. Universitat Pompeu Fabra.
discipline: philosophy (Heideggerian phenomenology) read through a sociological / critical-theory lens
thesis: Recovers Heidegger's account of boredom as 'a feeling of time' across its pre-history (Concept of Time 1924, Being and Time, FCM 1929-30, 'What is Metaphysics?') and then reads this ontological analysis sociologically: a lineage of cultural critique (Bloch, Adorno, Debord, Lipovetsky, Sloterdijk, with an aside to Zizek) shows the leisure/entertainment/spectacle economy manufacturing ever more efficient societal pastimes (Zeitvertreib) that manage, without dissolving, the ontological fear boredom discloses; even maximal comfort and fun 'can mask only partially the reach of that ontological fear.'

sections.title: Boredom's equivocal actuality
sections.summary: Heidegger's puzzle that boredom is familiar yet indefinable; Langeweile as 'long while'; boredom as 'a feeling of time' against a Kantian/Augustinian backdrop; Zeitvertreib, Sein-zum-Tode, horror vacui; pivots into 'What is Metaphysics?' on anxiety and the nothing.

sections.title: Metaphysics after the era of metaphysics
sections.summary: Anxiety and profound boredom as co-disclosive of nothingness; stages and qualifies the standard Heidegger/Frankfurt-School (Adorno) antagonism via their shared Nietzschean ground; FCM's 'Truth of Philosophy and its Ambiguity' passage; Husserl's method; closes on FCM's 'Awakening a Fundamental Attunement' chapter and its 'silent fog' leitmotif.

sections.title: 'Free time' and leisure in the spectacle's society
sections.summary: The sociological turn: Bloch's Principle of Hope on managed leisure-time as worker 'invigoration'; the 'permanent vacation' fantasy; smartphones extending pastime into every moment; Adorno on culture-industry pseudo-satisfaction; Debord's temps-marchandise; Lipovetsky's L'ere du vide; Kierkegaardian 'immediacy'.

sections.title: Roma o morte: ontological dilemmas inside the glasshouse
sections.summary: Names the 'boredom or fun' dilemma via Garibaldi's motto; Sorrentino's La Grande Bellezza (Orietta) as narcissistic self-representation-as-boredom-evasion; the postmodern self as 'reality show'; Sloterdijk's 'glasshouse'/'ether of comfort'; closes with David Foster Wallace's This Is Water.

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: central ontological anchor throughout; quotes FCM's own third-form rooting-in-time claim verbatim; never distinguished by name from forms I/II

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: vocabulary (drive-away/shake-off, Zeitvertreib) used generically for 'boredom' as such, unnamed as a distinct form

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: unnamed; the screen-mediated 'lonely together' scene reads as an implicit, uncredited instance of surface-occupied/depth-hollow boredom

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: organizing analytical move: sociologizes an ostensibly ontological, trait-like fundamental attunement as leisure-economy-produced and situational, without denying its ontological depth

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: not treated, and arguably run against: pastime diagnosed as symptomatic masking of boredom rather than adaptive/corrective regulation

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: touched via 'boredom or fun' (Roma o morte) dilemma and the absorbed-yet-lonely screen scene, without flow-theory vocabulary

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: horror vacui, nothingness-as-death; Lipovetsky's 'living without purpose or meaning'

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: second organizing construct; 'feeling of time'; depth explicitly decoupled from clock-duration

readings.claim: Boredom's ontological core is a disclosure of nothingness, anthropologically processed as death; the yawn and horror vacui are its bodily/affective symptoms.

The free-market leisure economy supplies options that pretend to be meaningful through the separation of working time and leisure time, manufacturing efficient societal pastimes (Bloch's worker 'invigoration', the 'permanent vacation' fantasy).

Heidegger and the Frankfurt-School critics (chiefly Adorno), despite their standard opposition, share more common ground than usually granted, traceable to a shared Nietzschean dissolution of metaphysical certainty.

Digital technology and social-media self-representation intensify rather than resolve the boredom-evasion dynamic: representation substitutes for 'the real,' so an experience is incomplete until shared and 'liked.'
The 'boredom or fun' alternative -- Zabalo's own coinage, a consumerist variation of Garibaldi's 'Roma o morte' -- names the operative motto of contemporary individualism.
Sloterdijk's 'glasshouse' names a privileged atmosphere of comfort in which boredom nonetheless persists as a restless guest, dependent for its reality on recognition by others.
Even at maximal comfort and entertainment, the desperate search for well-being and fun can mask only partially the reach of the ontological fear boredom discloses.

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin -- Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics
interlocutors.role: primary phenomenological source; feeling-of-time and profound-boredom material

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin -- The Concept of Time (1924) / Being and Time / What is Metaphysics?
interlocutors.role: pre-FCM and contemporaneous background architecture for boredom-as-temporality and anxiety/nothingness

interlocutors.name: Kant, Immanuel
interlocutors.role: time as a priori form of inner sense, read alongside Heidegger's phenomenological time

interlocutors.name: Augustine
interlocutors.role: Confessions Book XI quoted via Heidegger's Concept of Time on disposition/measuring time

interlocutors.name: Nietzsche, Friedrich
interlocutors.role: boredom quip (Beyond Good and Evil); credited by Heidegger as closing the epoch of metaphysics; common ground between Heidegger and Adorno

interlocutors.name: Adorno, Theodor W.
interlocutors.role: Frankfurt-School counterpoint; Philosophy of the New Music, Aesthetic Theory, Minima Moralia cited on culture-industry pseudo-satisfaction and art's negative function

interlocutors.name: Bloch, Ernst
interlocutors.role: The Principle of Hope cited on neoliberal management of leisure time ('invigoration', 'dull and desperate stroll')

interlocutors.name: Debord, Guy
interlocutors.role: The Society of the Spectacle cited on temps-marchandise / spectacular time

interlocutors.name: Lipovetsky, Gilles
interlocutors.role: L'ere du vide cited on postmodern individualism and living without purpose or meaning

interlocutors.name: Sloterdijk, Peter
interlocutors.role: Critique of Cynical Reason, Spheres III, In the Inner World of Capital cited; source of the 'glasshouse' metaphor

interlocutors.name: Kierkegaard, Soren
interlocutors.role: anxiety (via the 1929 lecture) and 'immediacy' (aesthetic stage) both traced to Kierkegaard

interlocutors.name: Zizek, Slavoj
interlocutors.role: cited (with a personal-interview aside) on the imperative to be happy / superego demand for satisfaction

interlocutors.name: Foster Wallace, David
interlocutors.role: This Is Water cited on adult-routine boredom as the essay's closing illustration

interlocutors.name: Bauman, Zygmunt
interlocutors.role: 'liquid' world/truth invoked in the post-truth discussion

interlocutors.name: Husserl, Edmund
interlocutors.role: phenomenological method credited as adopted by Heidegger for accessing Dasein/Being

tensions.axis: existential/ontological (Dasein-level, trait-like) vs. sociological/structural (leisure-economy-produced, situational) register for profound boredom
tensions.note: Zabalo's core organizing tension: does not resolve into a rejection of Heidegger's ontology, but argues the ontological structure is historically managed by a determinate socioeconomic apparatus.

tensions.axis: Heidegger vs. Frankfurt School (Adorno) -- standard antagonism vs. shared Nietzschean ground
tensions.note: Zabalo qualifies rather than resolves the standard opposition narrative, arguing the 'few coincidences...are not casual, but rather rooted on a common ground.'

tensions.axis: engaged surface behavior (screens, socializing, entertainment) vs. underlying persistent boredom
tensions.note: Structurally identical to fcm-05's surface-occupied/depth-hollow split, though Zabalo never names the second form.
